$comment: Machine-readable index of the theme/skin validation corpus. Source: eclipse-player.md §11.5. REQ-GEN-031 requires the desktop and Android engines to reach IDENTICAL verdicts on this corpus, so the verdicts live here rather than in either implementation's tests. `pipelineStep` is the REQ-THM-040 step that judges the fixture; the pipeline stops at the first failure, so a fixture is only ever a test of its own step. `schema` names the $id a JSON fixture is validated against, or null when the judge is code (path safety, SVG sanitisation, contrast, archive limits). `generated` replaces a committed file with a recipe both engines build identically — used for the multi-megabyte and 10,000-element cases. Verdicts: accept, reject, accept-with-warning (contrast, default settings), and table (the fixture is itself a list of sub-cases with their own verdicts).

pipelineSteps.3: manifest.json against its schema; checksum verification of every file
pipelineSteps.6: Every .eclayout against layout.schema.json, plus whitelist and budget checks
pipelineSteps.8: Every raster image probed for dimensions BEFORE decode
pipelineSteps.9: Fonts: format check, and fonts/LICENSE-fonts presence
pipelineSteps.10: Every EFS pattern parsed and its output cap verified

cases.reason: 9 fonts exceeds the limit of 8.
8193 x 8193 exceeds the 8192 x 8192 probe limit (REQ-LIB-068).
cases.note: Judged at step 8 by probing the header, BEFORE decode. A fixture that had to be decoded to be rejected would be the bug it is meant to catch.

cases.reason: 17 layout documents exceeds the limit of 16.
A single entry compressed 1024:1 exceeds the 100:1 limit.
2,001 entries exceeds the limit of 2,000.
One file over 8 MiB.
Total uncompressed size 32 MiB + 1 byte exceeds the 32 MiB limit.
A table of archive paths with the verdict path validation must return for each.
cases.note: 18 entries: 4 accept, 14 reject. Consumed by the installer's own test, not by a JSON-Schema run — which is why its verdict is `table`.

cases.reason: `minItems: 1` — a package that declares no capability does nothing.
`uniqueItems`.
`scripts` is not in the enum, and never will be (ADR 0003).
cases.note: The most valuable single line in this schema: the capability a malicious skin would want cannot be spelled.

cases.reason: Digest must be a string.
A SHA-256 is 64 hex characters.
Digests are lower-case hex so verification is a byte compare.
`minProperties: 3`: theme.json, LICENSE and preview.png are all mandatory.
BCP-47 shape: 2–3 letters plus optional subtags.
Required: without it the loader cannot refuse a package built for a newer app.
`checksums` is required — it is the integrity check, not an optimisation.
`const "preview.png"` — REQ-THM-015 fixes the name.
Four surfaces only; adding one is a schemaVersion change.
`additionalProperties: false`.
cases.note: Same reasoning as the theme: an install hook is exactly the member a hostile package would add.

cases.reason: Absolute path.
Backslash separator.
Control character.
Depth beyond the two segments the pattern allows.
Drive letter.
manifest.json is excluded from the pattern: it cannot checksum itself, and an entry claiming to is either confused or an attempt to make verification circular.
Embedded NUL, expressed in JSON as \u0000 — legal JSON, illegal path.
cases.note: Doubles as a parser test: §21.2's parser must carry the NUL through as a code point instead of truncating the string, or this fixture would appear to be the harmless `theme.json` and pass.

cases.reason: `maxLength: 200`.
`packagePath` is an allowlist pattern; traversal cannot match it.
cases.note: Defence in depth: step 2 already refused this path in the archive. The manifest is checked again because the two lists must agree, and a checksum map is itself a place to smuggle a path.

cases.reason: `bin/` is not a permitted top-level directory.
All five capabilities, three surfaces, i18n, fonts with their licence file.
cases.note: `fonts/LICENSE-fonts` is present because pipeline step 9 requires it whenever the fonts capability is used. The schema cannot express that dependency — it is a cross-file rule — so this fixture is what makes step 9 testable.

cases.reason: Theme-only package: the three mandatory files, one capability.
cases.note: `minProperties: 3` on checksums is exactly this package — theme.json, LICENSE, preview.png. A package cannot be smaller and still be well-formed.

cases.reason: AA or AAA.
Minimum 24. REQ-UIX-057's floor is not a skin's decision.
Not in the enum — and parallax is forbidden by design-system/motion.md.
cases.note: The token vocabulary and the motion rules agree; a value the design system bans is not reachable through the schema either.

cases.reason: Control points are clamped to [-2, 2]; 9 produces an unusable overshoot.
A cubic-bezier is exactly four numbers.
CSS colour names are not a colour.
Functional notation is not accepted.
`#fff` fails the colour pattern: 6 or 8 hex digits only.
cases.note: Shorthand is rejected rather than expanded. Accepting it would mean two spellings of one colour and a normalisation step before every comparison.

cases.reason: 2000 ms is the ceiling. A skin must not be able to make the UI feel broken.
offsetY, blur and color are all required.
`maxItems: 6` on the elevation ladder.
`color` requires background, surface, text, accent and border; `typography` is required at the root. This five-line theme cannot validate.
cases.note: A SPEC CONFLICT captured as a fixture, not smoothed over. REQ-THM-011 states that 'an author MUST be able to ship a five-line theme that only changes the accent colour'; the §11.2 schema transcribed verbatim into theme-schema.json forbids exactly that. The verdict recorded here is what the schema does TODAY. Resolving the conflict means a schema change — making `color`/`typography` and the inner `required` lists conditional on `extends` — which is a specification decision, not something an implementation may quietly assume. Logged in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md; when it is resolved this fixture moves to valid/ and its verdict flips to accept.

cases.reason: `fontStack` requires at least one family.
A font stack is an array, so fallbacks are explicit and ordered.
`setId` pattern is lower-case.
Minimum 0.5; 0 makes an outline icon invisible.
`id` must start and end alphanumeric.
`id` exceeds 64 characters.
`id` must be lower-case kebab.
cases.note: Case-insensitive filesystems make `Midnight` and `midnight` the same directory but different ids, which is how one skin overwrites another.

cases.reason: `color` is required.
`color.text` requires both primary and secondary.
cases.note: Two text roles are the minimum because §12.1's hierarchy needs a de-emphasised tone; a theme with only `primary` would force the app to invent one.

cases.reason: `mode` is light or dark. Following the system is an app setting that picks between two themes; it is not a third mode a theme can declare.
Opacity is a unit interval.
`full` is `const 9999` — the sentinel for a pill, not a number to tune.
cases.note: Fixing the value keeps `full` meaning 'fully rounded whatever the height', which a concrete radius cannot express.

cases.reason: `schemaVersion` is `const 1`; a future version must be refused by a v1 loader, not partially read.
`const 1` is the number 1, not the string.
`minItems: 4`.
`size` is the one required member of a type style.
`size` maximum is 96.
`scale` requires body and label.
cases.note: Those two carry nearly every string in the UI; the other five inherit.

cases.reason: Unknown member inside `color.text`.
cases.note: Roles are closed too. A skin cannot introduce a role the app never reads.

cases.reason: `additionalProperties: false` at the root.
cases.note: This is the schema doing ADR 0003's work: an unknown member is the shape a code-injection channel would take, so the format has no room for one.

cases.reason: The pattern is anchored; a pre-release suffix does not match.
cases.note: Deliberate: skin versions are compared numerically by the updater, and a pre-release ordering rule is a whole specification of its own.

cases.reason: `version` must be three dot-separated integers.
`minItems: 1` — an empty palette would render nothing.
`maxItems: 16`.
Absolute path.
A data: URI does not match the pattern either.
cases.note: Rejected even though it fetches nothing: an inline blob of arbitrary size bypasses the REQ-THM-017 per-file limit and the step-8 dimension probe, both of which work on package entries.

cases.reason: A URL would turn applying a theme into a network request — a fingerprinting beacon in a format that promises no network access.
Only images/, icons/ and fonts/ are asset directories.
`assetRef` allows one directory and a flat filename; no traversal fits.
cases.note: REQ-THM-012 calls this pattern a security control rather than a convenience, and this is the fixture that makes the claim testable.

cases.reason: UNC path.
Every token group populated; no unknown members.
cases.note: Values are taken from design-system/tokens.json so the fixture cannot drift away from §12.1. `emphasized` repeats the `standard` curve on purpose — §12.1 makes it emphatic by pairing that curve with the slow duration, not by defining a fifth curve.

cases.reason: Exactly the required members and nothing else.
cases.note: The floor of the format. Everything absent here inherits per REQ-THM-011, so this fixture also pins what 'unset' means: absent, not null. A null would be a type error.

cases.reason: 13 colour pairs with the exact ratio both engines must compute and the verdict for each of the two enforcement settings.
cases.note: A fourth directory beyond valid/invalid/malicious, because a contrast result is neither a schema pass nor an attack: it is a number that two engines must agree on. Recorded in this directory's README.

cases.reason: Schema-valid and installable; primary text on base background is 2.1946:1, well under the 4.5 floor, so the loader warns and names the offending pairs.
cases.note: The fixture that keeps step 4 and step 5 distinct. A validator that rejected this at the schema layer would be stricter than the specification and would make the 'Enforce accessible contrast' setting meaningless.

cases.reason: 21:1 on every text pair; meets the AAA target §29.1 requires of the High Contrast theme.
cases.note: `secondary` deliberately equals `primary`. A high-contrast theme has no room for a de-emphasised tone, and REQ-UIX-058's rule that meaning never rests on colour alone is what makes dropping the distinction acceptable here.

cases.reason: `assetRef` forbids traversal; only `images/` and `icons/` with a flat name match.
cases.note: On `source`, which is the assetRef. `icon` is a different field — a name resolved against the active icon set — and its own pattern admits no slash at all, so neither field can carry a path out of the package.

cases.reason: Maximum dimension is 16384.
`typeStyleRef` is one of the seven §12.1 tokens.
`icon` names an icon in the active set; a filename with a slash and an extension does not match its pattern.
cases.note: Easy for a skin author to get wrong, which is why it is a fixture: the error message must say 'icon name' and not 'invalid path'.

cases.reason: Node ids are identifier-shaped so validation messages can name them unambiguously.
`colorRef` requires a dotted token path; literal hex is rejected.
cases.note: A hard-coded colour would survive the REQ-THM-041 contrast check untouched and then look wrong under every other theme.

cases.reason: `root` is required.
`additionalProperties: false` on every node — an `on*` handler is unrepresentable.
cases.note: The layout DSL closes the same door the SVG sanitiser closes at step 7. Two formats, one rule.

cases.reason: The percentage pattern admits 0–100 only.
No functions in a predicate.
cases.note: A function library inside `when` would be a second expression language to harden, evaluated on every repaint.

cases.reason: No nesting beyond one level: the grammar admits a flat and/or chain, no parentheses.
cases.note: Flatness is what keeps predicate evaluation obviously linear and its error messages pointable at a single clause.

cases.reason: REQ-THM-030's grammar uses symbolic comparison operators; `greaterThan` is the smart-playlist spelling and does not belong here.
cases.note: The two grammars are close enough to confuse — the `when` predicate is a deliberately strict subset of the smart-playlist comparison grammar — and the operator vocabulary is where they differ. Worth a fixture precisely because the mistake reads as correct.

cases.reason: `const 1`.
Four surfaces only.
Actions are enum-only and mirror the §13.2 command registry.
`WebView` is not one of the 30 components.
cases.note: The closed vocabulary is the second half of ADR 0003: no unknown component means no escape hatch to a browser engine.

cases.reason: `bind` must name a whitelisted presentation-state path.
cases.note: The whitelist is why a skin cannot read anything the app did not choose to publish; a denylist here would leak on the first new field added.

cases.reason: Exercises 20 of the 30 components, both binding kinds, a `when` and an `enabledWhen` predicate, and one action per interactive node.
cases.note: Every interactive node carries `accessibleName` or a `tooltip`, because REQ-UIX-063 makes them the same string and REQ-TST-019 tests for a non-empty accessible name. A skin that omitted them would validate against the schema and fail accessibility, so this fixture is the shape a reviewer should copy.

cases.reason: The REQ-THM-031 worked example from §11.4, transcribed so the specification's own illustration is a test.
cases.note: Binds `settings.showMiniVisualizer`, which is the case REQ-THM-027 and REQ-THM-031 disagree about: the former says the state model exposes no settings values, the latter binds one. layout.schema.json follows the narrowest reading that keeps both true — a short allowlist of presentation-affecting settings only. Because this fixture comes from the spec verbatim, it is also the evidence for that reading.

cases.reason: Entity expansion bomb: 10^8 characters from 700 bytes.
cases.note: REQ-THM-042 requires entity expansion be DISABLED, so the defence is that the expansion never starts — not a size limit reached after some of it has happened. The fixture is small on purpose: a validator that survives it by hitting a memory cap has still failed the requirement.

cases.reason: Any DOCTYPE declaration, even this entirely conventional one.
cases.note: Rejected without inspecting what it references. A DOCTYPE is where entity declarations live, and a validator that allows 'harmless' DOCTYPEs has to decide which ones are harmless — a decision with a long history of being got wrong. The cost is that legitimate exports from older editors are refused; the fix belongs in the authoring tool, and docs/SKIN-AUTHORING.md says so.

cases.reason: 10,001 elements exceeds REQ-THM-042's cap of 10,000.
cases.note: Generated by the test runner from the recipe above rather than committed: the file is ~50 KB of noise and both engines can build it identically from three numbers. Committing it would also invite someone to 'tidy' it.

cases.reason: External entity pointing at a local file — classic XXE.
`<foreignObject>` embeds a whole other document type — an HTML renderer reached through an icon file.
Any `href` that is not an internal fragment — a clickable icon that navigates.
Protocol-relative href.
cases.note: A check for a `http`/`https` prefix misses this one; the correct test is that the value is a `data:` URI or an internal fragment, everything else refused.

cases.reason: `<image>` with a non-`data:` href. REQ-THM-042 permits `data:` here and nothing else.
Quadratic blowup: one modest entity referenced many times, which stays under naive depth limits while still expanding 400 KB.
Unclosed element: not well-formed XML.
cases.note: Rejected rather than recovered. HTML-style error recovery is how one parser's view of a document diverges from another's, and the sanitiser's view must be the renderer's view exactly.

cases.reason: `OnClIcK` is the same attribute: XML attribute names are case-sensitive but HTML event handlers are matched case-insensitively by browsers and by Qt's SVG renderer.
cases.note: The rule must be applied case-insensitively or the denylist is trivially bypassed.

cases.reason: A prefixed event attribute. The check is on the local name, not the qualified name.
Any `on*` event attribute.
Parameter entity fetching an external DTD — the out-of-band XXE variant used to exfiltrate when the response is not echoed back.
Same element wrapped in CDATA.
cases.note: Present because a regex-based sanitiser that looks for `<script>` followed by text can be fooled by the CDATA wrapper. Sanitisation must run on a parsed tree.

cases.reason: `<script>` is named first in REQ-THM-042's strip-and-reject list.
`<style>` containing `@import`: the same network fetch through CSS.
`file://` through the legacy xlink attribute — local file read, not just a fetch.
`<use>` with an external reference: a network fetch at paint time.
Entity expanded inside an attribute value rather than text content.
cases.note: Some parsers guard text nodes and not attributes.

cases.reason: Survives sanitisation byte-for-byte: no script, no external reference, no DOCTYPE, 8 elements.
cases.note: `fill="url(#g1)"` is an INTERNAL fragment reference and must be kept. A sanitiser that strips every `url(...)` breaks legitimate gradients, so the accept side of the rule needs a fixture as much as the reject side does.

cases.reason: Exactly 10,000 elements is within the cap.
cases.note: The boundary pair matters more than either side alone: an off-by-one here either rejects a legal icon set or admits an unbounded one.

cases.reason: Schema-valid: `efs` is a string and the pattern is syntactically fine. Step 10 is the judge, not step 6.
cases.note: A DELIBERATE two-verdict fixture. REQ-EFS-009 caps rendered output at 4096 characters, so at runtime this pattern is harmless — it truncates. REQ-THM-040 step 10 nonetheless requires every EFS pattern's 'output cap verified' at install time, which is only meaningful if a pattern that would exceed the cap is REFUSED rather than silently clipped. Both readings are defensible: refusing tells the author, clipping keeps a working skin working. The stricter one is recorded here because a skin whose text is invisibly truncated is a bug report nobody can diagnose. Logged in docs/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md.
